forces.title: Demand for sovereign AI capacity challenges offshore models
forces.description: Governments around the world are increasingly prioritizing domestically located and controlled AI training and computing power capacity. This significant structural shift is driven by escalating concerns over national security, stringent data-residency mandates, and evolving regulatory frameworks. For UK multinational corporations, this trend could necessitate a re-evaluation of their Global Capability Centre (GCC) strategy. It may lead to increased reliance on local operators or joint ventures within their home country for highly sensitive AI workloads, potentially diverting investments away from established offshore GCCs in India. This could also result in higher operational costs for maintaining compliance if new data localization requirements are broadly enforced across critical functions currently handled by Indian GCCs, posing a considerable strategic risk.
forces.source_title: The Digital Infrastructure Universe Continues to Expand. Here's How to Benefit.

forces.title: Data sovereignty demands push for in-country IT capacity
forces.description: Regulatory bodies in numerous countries are tightening data sovereignty and residency requirements, significantly increasing the imperative for in-country or in-region data center capacity to handle specific sensitive workloads. This presents a notable headwind for UK multinational corporations that leverage Global Capability Centres (GCCs) located in India for their data-intensive operations. Such evolving regulations could compel these companies to either repatriate certain critical functions or establish new regional GCCs closer to the parent entity or target markets, specifically to ensure compliance. This shift would inevitably lead to increased operational complexity and potentially substantial costs as companies adapt their global delivery models to meet these stringent new legislative demands, impacting the long-term viability of some offshore services.
